top_signals.title: Nakhle: Oil Volatility to Stay Until Iran Endgame Clear
top_signals.summary: Brent held around $101 per barrel as Iran vowed it was prepared for a more intense war after hostilities flared across the Middle East. But Carole Nakhle, CEO of Crystol Energy told Bloomberg’s Jennifer Zabasajja on Horizons Middle East & Africa $101/b is not as high a threshold as it could have been. (Source: Bloomberg)
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.

top_signals.title: Oil Holds Above $100 as U.S.-Iran Tanker War Escalates
top_signals.summary: Crude oil prices held near recent highs after rallying sharply earlier this week, with gains driven by an escalation in the U.S.-Iran conflict and intensifying attacks on tankers in the Persian Gulf. Iran reported hits on U.S. warships and tankers in the Persian Gulf, while the U.S. said it had hit ten Iranian tankers. At the time of writing, Brent crude was trading at $101.04 per barrel and West Texas Intermediate at $96.09 per barrel. Iran has signaled U.S. attacks on its tankers will prompt further escalation. top_signals.title: Forced Into the Right Decision? A Look at U.S. Land-Based Deterrence Posture
top_signals.summary:
In 2019, Steve Fetter wrote “A Cheaper Nuclear Sponge,” in which he argued that building a new intercontinental ballistic missile (ICBM) was unnecessary for strengthening U.S. land-based deterrence. After several years of changing defense budgets and strategic priorities, we asked Steve to revisit his arguments.Image: U.S. Air Force (John Ingle)In your 2019 article, you argued that building an entirely new ICBM was unnecessary and that the Pentagon could save tens of billions by extending the life of the Minuteman III instead.
